target.title: fix(auto-reply): prevent block-reply coalescer from dropping tail text on abort/stop
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram DM block-streaming (`streaming.mode="block"`) silently drops the tail of long assistant replies. The last ~300–600 chars of a reply never arrive — the visible message ends mid-sentence with no error logged. (Issue #102578)

## Why This Change Was Made

Root cause in `createBlockReplyCoalescer` (`src/auto-reply/reply/block-reply-coalescer.ts`):

1. **`flush({force:true})` at turn finalization was skipped by `shouldAbort()`** — when a prior block delivery had timed out during streaming, `aborted = true` was set in the pipeline (`block-reply-pipeline.ts`). The final force-flush then saw `shouldAbort() === true`, reset the buffer, and silently dropped the buffered tail text.

2. **`stop()` at pipeline boundary didn't reach `onBlockReply` after abort** — on error/recovery paths only `stop()` was called without a prior `flush()`. Any remaining buffered text below `minChars` was lost downstream when `sendPayload` returned early due to the `aborted` flag.

3. **No warning when text was discarded** — the silent data loss had no log trace.

### Fix architecture

Two-part fix that separates concerns cleanly:

**Coalescer layer** (`block-reply-coalescer.ts`):
- `flush({force:true})` now bypasses `shouldAbort()` — the caller explicitly requested data delivery.
- `stop()` only clears the idle timer; it no longer flushes. The pipeline owns drain before stop.
- `logVerbose` warning when abort discards buffered text, with context on force vs non-force flush.

**Pipeline layer** (`block-reply-pipeline.ts`):
- `sendPayload()` gained a third `bypassAbort` parameter. Coalescer-sourced payloads (via `onFlush`) pass `bypassAbort = true` so force-flushed tail text reaches `onBlockReply` even after the pipeline is marked `aborted`.
- The coalescer already gates abort independently via `shouldAbort()`; overlapping it at the pipeline level was the bug.

## User Impact

- **Before**: Telegram DM users with `streaming.mode="block"` lose the final ~300–600 chars of long replies silently, with no error or retry.
- **After**: The complete reply is delivered. All buffered text is flushed on finalization. If text is discarded via non-force flush during abort, a verbose log entry explains what was dropped.

## Evidence

### Unit test results

**New tests** (`src/auto-reply/reply/block-reply-coalescer.test.ts` — 9 tests, all passing):
- `force=true` bypasses `shouldAbort` — buffered text is flushed
- `stop()` does NOT flush; only clears idle timer
- `hasBuffered()` returns true after `stop()` when buffer has text
- `flush({force:false})` preserves default idle behavior
- `flush({force:true})` sends buffer even when under minChars
- Full pipeline simulation: tail text preserved across finalization
- Abort without force discards buffer
- Accumulated text >= maxChars triggers immediate flush

**Pipeline integration tests (all passing)**:
- `block-reply-pipeline.test.ts` — 26 pass
- Combined: 35 tests passing across coalescer + pipeline suites

### How the test proves the real scenario

The `full pipeline simulation` test replicates the exact gateway flow:
1. Stream large blocks accumulating without exceeding `maxChars`
2. Add the critical tail text that would previously be lost
3. Call `flush({force:true})` then `stop()` simulating finalization
4. Assert all accumulated text including the tail is delivered

### Logging

When abort discards buffered text, a `logVerbose` entry records the exact char count and whether the flush was forced or cancelled — enabling operators to detect silent data loss in production.

## How The Fix Was Tested

All tests pass with the latest `origin/main`.
No import cycles (`pnpm check:import-cycles`: 0 cycles).
Changed files: `block-reply-coalescer.ts`, `block-reply-pipeline.ts`, `block-reply-coalescer.test.ts` (net -2 LOC).

## Related

- Fixes #102578
